# ADR 0004: Milestone 3 decisions

- **Status:** draft, sections are added as each stage lands.
- **Date:** 2026-10-09
- **Decider:** lodmaome. Drafted with AI assistance (Claude).
- **Evidence:** outside the repository, in `C:\git\conduit-env-evidence\m3-evidence\` (cited by name only).

## 1. Release check 16: a scan of every reachable commit

**Why.** The earlier secret check (11) reads the tree. A secret that an old commit held and a later commit removed is invisible to it and still public once the history is pushed. Pushing makes the history public-readable the day the repository is made public, so the history is scanned first.
**What it scans** (`tools/lib/history-scan.mjs`, `git log -p --all`, every added line of every reachable commit; every commit message; every path ever touched; the 50 largest blobs): JWT-shaped strings, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_` and `github_pat_` tokens, AWS access key ids, private key blocks, credential assignments and URL credentials other than the documented local database password `0000` (exempt by value, as in check 11),
and files that should never be public (`.tar`, `.tgz`, `.zip`, `.gz`, `.7z`, `.dump`, `.sql`, `.sqlite`, `.har`, `.pem`, `.p12`, `.pfx`, a root `.env`, anything inside a folder named `*-evidence`) and any blob over 1 MB. The gate's own two fixture files are exempt, as in check 11. Findings name the kind, the short commit and the path, never the matched text.
**Local mode** (`node tools/release-gate.mjs env-vN --local`) also looks for this machine's Windows user name (derived at run time from `os.userInfo()`, never written into a tracked file; whole-word and case-insensitive, so a longer name that merely starts with it does not match) and for Windows home-directory paths as findings, and lists `C:\git\...` paths as information (the documents cite the evidence folder on purpose).
**Tests** (`m3-evidence\s0\selftest-check16.txt`, seen): the golden control passes; seven failing fixtures (a token in an old commit, a non-documented password in an old commit, a tar, an evidence folder, a 5 MB blob, the user name, a Windows home-directory path); a presence control inside the check (a probe token in a probe "old commit" and a probe tar path must be found, or the check refuses to pass);
and a real throwaway repository whose old commit holds a fake token (built at run time) that a later commit removed: the HEAD tree is clean, the history scan finds the token, normal mode does not report the user name, local mode does.
**Result on the real history** (`m3-evidence\s0\release-gate-normal.txt`, `release-gate-local.txt`, seen): 40 commits, 173 path entries, no finding; the largest blob is 61,150 bytes; local mode: no finding, 13 information lines about `C:\git\...` paths. Not rewriting history was not needed.

## 2. The three workflows and release check 17

**Files.** `.github/workflows/env-verify-core.yml` (reusable, `workflow_call`, no `ENV_CANONICAL` guard because attempts call it), `env-verify.yml` (the environment's wrapper: push to `main`, pull requests, manual dispatch; guarded by `vars.ENV_CANONICAL == 'true'`, not by a repository-name slug), `env-pin-drift.yml` (weekly cron at 05:17 on Mondays and manual dispatch, same guard, read-only, runs `node tools/pin-drift.mjs`).
All three match `env/OWNED.txt` (`.github/workflows/env-*.yml`). `actionlint` and `yamllint` now lint them for real: 3 files clean (`m3-evidence\s0\gate-with-workflows.txt`, seen; the earlier "0 files" SKIP is gone).

**What the core does:** checks out with full history (the release gate scans every commit), sets up Node pinned exactly to 22.23.1 (the version measured locally; whether `actions/setup-node` can install that exact version is **not seen yet**, it will be on the first run), records the runner (OS, what `/bin/sh` is, Docker, Compose, Node, Chrome), probes Chrome's sandbox,
starts the stack with `docker compose -f compose.yaml up -d --wait` (the bypass), then runs `node tools/verify.mjs`, `sh tools/gate.sh` and `node --test`, and, only when the caller passes `run-release-gate`, the release gate for the newest `## env-vN` heading of `docs/env/CHANGELOG.md` plus its self-test. On failure it prints `docker compose ps` and the last 100 log lines of each service; it uploads no artifact, so no third action is used.
**Chrome** floats with the runner image: its version is recorded in the log, not pinned. **Chrome's sandbox on ubuntu-24.04 is unverified** (a likely problem, not seen): `tools/browser-check.mjs` starts Chrome with `--no-sandbox` only if `CONDUIT_CHROME_NO_SANDBOX=1`; the core exposes this as the explicit input `chrome-no-sandbox` (default `false`), and the sandbox probe step logs whether Chrome starts with its sandbox. If the rehearsal shows it is needed, the wrapper sets the input and this section says so.
**A calling job cannot carry `timeout-minutes`** (GitHub allows only a few keys on a job that calls a reusable workflow), so the wrapper's `core` job has none and the called job has `timeout-minutes: 30`; release check 17 accepts that and requires a timeout on every job that does not call a reusable workflow.

**Rules enforced for every workflow (release check 17, `tools/lib/release-checks.mjs`):** every `uses:` is pinned by a full 40-hex commit SHA with its tag in a trailing comment and has a row in `THIRD-PARTY.md` carrying the repository and the first 12 hex characters of the SHA; a top-level `permissions:` (here `contents: read` only); `timeout-minutes` on every job that runs steps; no `pull_request_target`; no use of `secrets` (comments are ignored).
Seven failing fixtures (unpinned, SHA without tag comment, no THIRD-PARTY row, no permissions, no timeout, `pull_request_target`, a secret) and a golden control pass the self-test (`selftest-workflows.txt`, seen). With no workflow files the check prints SKIP, never a silent pass.
**Actions pinned** (tag-to-commit checked with `git ls-remote`, `s0\action-pins.txt`, seen): `actions/checkout` v7.0.1 `3d3c42e5aac5...` and `actions/setup-node` v7.1.0 `949feb2413d6...`, both lightweight tags, both MIT (LICENSE read at those commits, `s0\lic\`), both declare `using: node24`. The newest stable tags listed on 2026-10-09 were chosen; whether the runner supports Node 24 actions is **not seen yet**.

**`tools/pin-drift.mjs`** compares each repository pin with `git ls-remote <repo> HEAD` and each image pin with the top-level digest of `docker buildx imagetools inspect <name:tag>`; for the derived `FRONTEND_REALWORLD_SHA` it prints SKIP. Unit tests: parsers, a control (no drift, exit 0), an outdated-pin fixture (two DRIFT rows, exit 2) and an unreadable remote (ERROR rows, exit 2). Real run, read-only, today: 11 comparable pins, 0 drift (`s0\pin-drift-real.txt`, seen).
Floating tags (`postgres:18`, `nginx:1-alpine`, `python:3.12-slim-bookworm`) will eventually drift, and then the weekly run fails visibly by design.

## 3. Check 16 scans what will be pushed

**Decision (lodmaome, at G0).** A history scan that also reads local backup branches would fail on a branch that is never pushed. By default check 16 now scans `refs/heads/main` and every tag (`refs/tags/*`), which is exactly what a push of `main` and of tags makes public; `--all-refs` scans every ref. The CI core keeps the default. Every push in Milestone 3 names its refspec (`main`, or the rehearsal branch), never `--all`, and `backup/pre-rewrite` is never pushed.
**Tests** (`m3-evidence\s0\selftest-allrefs.txt`, seen): in a throwaway repository (default branch `main`), a token that an old commit of `main` held and a later commit removed is still found by the default scan; a token that exists only on a branch `backup/x` is **not** found by the default scan and **is** found with `--all-refs`; the golden control passes.
**Real use** (`s0\r-local-main.txt`, `r-local-allrefs.txt`, seen): on `main` after the rewrite, local mode finds nothing (44 commits, 191 path entries, largest blob 61,150 bytes); with `--all-refs` it finds the two items that only `backup/pre-rewrite` still holds, which shows the flag reaches the other refs.

**The history rewrite that preceded it (lodmaome's decision (a)).** The first local-mode run found this machine's Windows user name and a home-directory path example in my own ADR 0004 text, in a local, never-pushed commit. The five local commits after `a113f62` were rewritten non-interactively: a new branch from `a113f62`, `git cherry-pick` of the check 16 commit, the one-line fix cherry-picked on top with `-n` and folded in with `git commit --amend --no-edit`, then the next three original commits cherry-picked, the fix commit itself dropped, and `main` replaced by a branch rename.
Why this method: cherry-pick keeps each commit's author, author date, message and trailer byte for byte (checked), needs no interactive editor, and uses no `reset`. `backup/pre-rewrite` (local only, never pushed) still holds the old five. Proof in `s0\rewrite-proof.txt` (seen): 44 commits; `git diff backup/pre-rewrite HEAD` empty; the four rewritten commits have identical author, author date, subject and body; no tracked file cites an old hash; no whole-word match of the user name on `main`.
